budget_items.topic: Citizens' petition override at town meeting
budget_items.what_was_said: The chair listed two excluded-debt articles and a citizens' petition for a Proposition 2.5 override among the warrant articles voters will decide at town meeting.

The town manager reported the House Ways and Means budget recommends Chapter 70 funded higher than last year with unrestricted government aid level-funded, producing a net increase to Lunenburg's planned aid.
The town manager said residents can buy a pre-bagged town-meeting lunch from the school department.
The Green Communities Committee chair described the grant award and how much of it went toward heat pumps versus other projects like cruisers and refrigeration units.

The committee chair broke down the full project quote for the school heat-pump/central-control retrofit, the grant and rebate portions contingent on the central system, and what would remain for the town if the central unit were skipped.
The committee chair said the town has received close to that much in state grant funding to date through the program.
The chair and committee compared the town's prior monthly street-light bill to the current cost after the LED/Unitil conversion.
The board discussed having the school committee chair, rather than a select board member, move the warrant article transferring free cash to the school since he would answer related questions.
The town manager reported a minor correction to the sewer enterprise budget article related to indirect costs, already fixed in the printed warrant book.

decisions.decision: Board directed staff to press the Ritter building roof/gutter contractor to begin work before the April 30 extension deadline rather than granting another extension without progress.

Board agreed in principle to change the Green Communities Committee's associate members to alternates (or otherwise let associates vote to make quorum), pending confirmation from town counsel that it is legal.

Board agreed the town manager should connect key department heads with the Green Communities Committee over the summer, before the capital plan process, so energy-grant options are considered earlier.
Board decided to leave warrant articles 27 (PEG access/cable), 32 and 33 (board of assessors items) on the consent calendar as-is rather than pulling them off in advance.

Board agreed that going forward, non-select-board officials (e.g., parks commission chair, school committee chair) and citizen petitioners should move their own warrant articles at town meeting rather than always having a select board member do it.
Board agreed to schedule a standby meeting ahead of town meeting in case deferred articles need board action, even if it may end up not being needed.

minutes.headline: Select Board finalized the town meeting warrant, including a roughly $49M budget and a citizen override question.
minutes.summary: The Select Board reviewed and approved the annual town meeting consent calendar, discussed which officials should move which warrant articles (including an override petition, a school free-cash transfer, and Marshall Park), and heard a Green Communities Committee report on heat-pump grant funding and street-light savings. Town manager updates covered FY26 state aid, project timelines, and staffing vacancies, and a resident used public comment to object to holding town meeting on a Saturday.

what_happened.line: The Select Board approved the annual town meeting warrant as amended, including the budget and a citizen-petition override question, by unanimous voice vote.
The board decided that going forward, non-select-board officials and citizen petitioners will move their own warrant articles, including the school free-cash transfer and Marshall Park.
The town manager reported the state's House budget raises Chapter 70 aid while level-funding unrestricted aid, a net increase to Lunenburg's planned state aid.
The board pushed the Ritter building roof and gutter contractor to start work before the April 30 deadline rather than granting another extension.
A resident used public comment to object to holding town meeting on a Saturday, citing conflicts with religious observance and children's events.

why_it_matters: The approved warrant is what residents will vote on at town meeting, including the operating budget and an override question that could raise taxes above the levy limit.
Moving the school free-cash transfer and Marshall Park articles away from select board members changes who answers questions on the town meeting floor for those items.
A shift in state Chapter 70 and unrestricted aid changes how much of the school budget the town has to cover from local taxes.
